text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures were slightly higher in late trade, spending a second day more closely following U.S. economic fundamentals than events closer to home. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.42, down 0.12 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - December gilt futures ended a volatile day on Wednesday a quarter of a point down from Tuesday's close, after the Bank of England raised official interest rates a quarter of a point to six percent. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-15/32, down 10/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures took their lead from German and U.S. bond markets again on Wednesday, settling lower after a relatively volatile session in which U.S. economic data set the tone. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.20 down 0.10 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures generally headed south in late trade although the most traded 10-year July Btp closed a few ticks up on the day. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 122.65 down 0.12 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - The U.S. Treasuries' rally stopped dead in its tracks midday Wednesday, as a smaller- than-expected decline in new home sales gave players an excuse to take profits, traders said. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-12/32, down 07/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.71 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended Wednesday's Tokyo session sharply higher, boosted by strong buying interest in both cash and futures, traders said. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 125.23, up 0.63 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - European currencies continued to dominate the Eurobond market, with French francs particularly prominent.
Adding further supply to the ten-year sector the European Investment Bank issued a 1.0 billion franc step-up bond and Landesgirokasse launched a 2.0 billion franc straight deal.
Yesterday, Spain added 3.0 billion francs to a 10-year bond launched in July which was widely considered to have been priced too tightly.
Today's deals were said to provide little interest to investors because there had been too much similar supply.
